reason: The cited evidence shows that nanoprecipitates can enable adaptive glaze formation and ultralow wear in a different alloy (E1, E2), and that Y2O3 refines oxide scale in coatings (E3), but no evidence supports the specific claim that Y2O3 nanoprecipitates will form uniformly in CoCrFeNi, pin grain boundaries, and catalyze a lubricious glaze across the full temperature range. The key premises about Y2O3 dispersion, Zener pinning, and glaze catalysis in this specific system are unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Y2O3 nanoprecipitates can be uniformly dispersed in a CoCrFeNi matrix by adding 1–2 at% Y
Y2O3 nanoprecipitates will pin grain boundaries via Zener pinning, preventing coarsening at low temperatures
Pre-dispersed Y2O3 nanoprecipitates will catalyze formation of a protective nanocrystalline oxide glaze at high temperatures
The dual mechanism (grain pinning + adaptive glaze) will yield low friction (<0.3) and ultralow wear (10^-7–10^-6 mm³/Nm) from RT to 800 °C
